questions.question: Define the term 'glocalisation' and give one example. (4 marks)

BellaVita is an Italian cosmetics brand expanding into the Middle East and East Asia. Its marketing features European models and emphasises Italian luxury heritage. Analyse the challenges of marketing in culturally diverse markets. (6 marks)

A Swiss watchmaker produces handmade luxury timepieces priced between £10,000 and £50,000, selling through exclusive retailers in 30 countries to approximately 5,000 buyers per year. Assess the extent to which a global niche strategy can be more profitable than a mass market approach. (10 marks)

A major American fast-food chain has seen strong success in Japan and the UK but significant difficulties in India and several African markets. Evaluate the extent to which cultural differences are the most significant barrier to successful global marketing. (20 marks)
Outline two ways Ansoff's Matrix can be applied to international business expansion. (4 marks)

Source A. Serana is a Singaporean skincare brand sold in 6 countries. It runs one advertising campaign in all of them, which cost $1.2m; a separate campaign for each country would cost about $450,000. Its directors now plan to enter Zarand, a hot, dry country where most people are Muslim and speak their own language. In Zarand most skincare is bought in small family shops and online, and cheap local creams are popular. Spoken in Zarand's language, the name Serana sounds close to the word for "slippery". Serana also makes a halal-certified, alcohol-free serum for Muslim buyers. It estimates the number of likely buyers in five countries at 40,000, 25,000, 60,000, 15,000, 20,000. Each buyer uses 3 bottles a year at $30 a bottle, against $20 for a mass-market serum. Its current options include taking its existing moisturiser to Zarand, and launching a new hair-care range there. Explain one way Ansoff's matrix could help Serana decide whether to enter Zarand. (4 marks)
